title: 'All men' means Gospel hearers in external communion — even the vicious — not only the faithful
source_text: CXLIII. Sed nihil opus fuit viro docto hic citare Paraeum. Nam ipsae meae Theses, quas illi carpere libuit, integrae fere in eo insumuntur, ut probent secundum communem Reformatorum doctrinam, 1. Fideles singulos absque speciali revelatione, posse certo credere se esse in Dei gratia: 2. Fideles singulos, non tantum posse, sed etiam debere ea de re certo persuasos esse; & si de eo certi non sint, istud quendam defectum & quandam infirmitatem, in eorum fide arguere: 3. Denique Certitudinem illam communiter apud Reformatos certitudinem fidei vocari. Itaque vir Doctus in sua conjectura fallitur. Nam per omnes & singulos homines, non intellexi solummodo omnes & singulos fideles. Nec tamen mens mea fuit Reformatos accusari ab Ecclesiae Romanae Doctoribus, quod doceant omnes homines in universum, absque ulla exceptione, teneri certo credere se esse in Dei gratia. Verum per omnes & singulos homines intellexi omnes & singulos quibus annuntiatur Evangelium, & qui sunt in externa Ecclesiae communione; etiamsi alioqui flagitiose vivant & vitiis indulgeant.
pass_a_gloss: But there was no need for the learned man here to cite Pareus. For my very Theses which it pleased him to carp at are almost wholly spent in proving according to the common doctrine of the Reformers: 1. that each of the faithful without special revelation can certainly believe that he is in the grace of God; 2. that each of the faithful not only can but also ought to be certainly persuaded of that matter; and if they are not certain of it, that argues a certain defect and a certain infirmity in their faith; 3. finally that that certainty is commonly called among the Reformed the certainty of faith. Therefore the Learned Man errs in his conjecture. For by all and each men I did not understand only all and each of the faithful. Nor yet was my mind that the Reformed are accused by the Doctors of the Roman Church of teaching that all men universally, without any exception, are bound certainly to believe that they are in the grace of God. But by all and each men I understood all and each to whom the Gospel is announced, and who are in the external communion of the Church — even if otherwise they live flagitiously and indulge vices.
pass_b_english: Pareus was unnecessary: Le Blanc's own theses already prove Reformed common doctrine that each of the faithful can and ought be certain of grace without special revelation, and that such certainty is commonly called faith-certainty — so lack of it marks infirmity, not unbelief of the fundamentals.
The opponent's conjecture fails: 'all and each men' did not mean only the faithful.
Nor did Le Blanc mean Rome charges a duty on absolutely every human without exception; he meant all Gospel hearers in external church communion — even the vicious.

choices.english: I did not understand only the faithful
choices.why: Key semantic defense of Thesis I wording.
